opportunities.title: Small Grants

amount.raw: Awards vary according to project but will only exceptionally exceed £6,000 and will generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000. Travel: up to £2,000 per person for trips up to 13 days, up to £2,500 per person for 14 days or more; PhD fieldwork visits of six months+ up to £5,000; Japan office up to ¥300,000 for PhD travel.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications are not accepted from individuals for personal projects. Applications from PhD students must include a letter of support from their supervisor. Projects originating in the UK go through the UK office; those originating in Japan through the Japan office.
opportunities.summary: Seed funding enabling UK-Japan projects that deepen mutual understanding and collaboration across any field including arts and culture, humanities and social issues, Japanese language, medicine and health, science, youth and education, and sport. Supports events, exchanges, collaborative projects, teaching/development of Japanese language and cultural studies, and academic research/visits.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

amount.raw: Up to £10,000 per award; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally show an existing research record, but consideration also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields establishing working links between organisations or producing a publishable comparative study. Preference given to those not previously involved in UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants. Applications submitted to the London office regardless of where based.
opportunities.summary: Supports exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK, including study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare. Grants may be used for travel expenses or contribute to other costs including conference and publication costs. Projects must involve partners in both the UK and Japan.
